A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FFGo research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original video-generation experiments and a user study with 200 annotations from 40 participants, including numerical results in Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds automatic quantitative results in Table 2 and qualitative comparisons and analyses in the appendix.

M1.justification: The data-curation pipeline, first-frame composition, LoRA adaptation, transition trigger, and removal of initial transition frames remain unchanged. The arbitrary unique-trigger explanation clarifies the existing procedure without introducing a new component.

E1.justification: The training corpus and original 50-case application coverage are retained. Appendix F adds evaluation under swapped, reordered, and overlapping first-frame layouts, extending the tested input conditions. The clarification that references come from different sources does not establish a changed dataset.

E2.justification: Appendix B and Figure 8 add an evaluated MS-Diffusion + I2V pipeline as a qualitative comparator. Wan2.2-I2V-A14B, VACE, and SkyReels-A2 remain the main baselines and also appear in the new automatic-metric comparison.

E3.justification: v1's quantitative evaluation uses human ratings and rankings. v2 adds a complementary automatic evaluation covering identity, text alignment, motion, and perceptual quality through seven CLIP/DINO and VBench metrics. Appendix F also introduces layout-variation tests. Existing training settings and the user-study protocol remain unchanged; the additions do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds illustrative tests of unseen-layout robustness (Figure 16), delayed subject entry against a two-stage pipeline (Figure 8), and shadow consistency across reference sources (Figure 17). These address additional questions through limited qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new automatic scores retain point-value reporting, and the user-study annotation and participant counts are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, including FFGo's 4.28 overall-quality rating and 81.2% first-place selections. New Table 2 substantially expands the quantitative findings: FFGo leads CLIP-cap (34.00), motion smoothness (0.98), dynamic degree (14.64), and imaging quality (0.73), and ties VACE on DINO-I (0.46). It trails VACE on CLIP-I (0.67 versus 0.68) and aesthetic quality (0.85 versus 0.92). Figures 8, 16, and 17 add qualitative results; Figure 5 replaces the displayed SkyReels-A2 and VACE sequences without documenting whether they were rerun.

T1.justification: The LoRA equations and generation formulation in Section 3 are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the new appendix explanations introduce no mathematical derivations or assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: the first frame acts as a conceptual memory buffer, and lightweight adaptation using 20–50 examples enables broad customization without architectural changes. Additional evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: New appendix passages interpret layout results as contextual understanding, attribute cross-source visual consistency to pretrained priors, and explain temporal-control advantages over fixed-layout two-stage pipelines. The existing limitations concerning reference count, resolution, and selective control remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly clarifies that the 50 test reference sets combine materials from different sources and that the transition phrase may be arbitrary provided it is unique. These refine existing documentation. Hardware, training duration, LoRA rank, optimizer settings, resolutions, prompt templates, and project-page access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds DreamBooth as inspiration for unique triggers and positions FFGo against MS-Diffusion-based two-stage generation. It also adds citations on image-layer decomposition and audiovisual video generation. The broader related-work narrative remains intact; numerous other reference edits update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely unchanged, with localized trigger and test-set clarifications, affiliation edits, and an added acknowledgment. Short appendix sections expand the discussion while retaining the earlier supplementary content and its organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 2 and Figures 8, 16, and 17, and replaces two baseline image sequences in Figure 5. Existing supplementary Figures 8–14 become Figures 9–15 and are reflowed. The main figure and table designs remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful complementary quantitative evidence and targeted comparisons addressing temporal control and layout robustness. Table 2 also makes performance tradeoffs visible, including FFGo trailing VACE on CLIP-I and aesthetics. These additions improve the empirical account, but sparse automatic-evaluation details and illustrative qualitative tests limit the strength of the gain.
